Medical Oncology Follow-up
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (L2, L4) on leuprolide q12 weeks and enzalutamide 160 mg daily since 10/2023.
Interval: left eye vein occlusion in November, followed by retina. No bone pain. Energy fair.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: ECOG 1. No spinal tenderness.
PSA 0.1 ng/mL.
Plan: continue current therapy; leuprolide today. Next PSA April; visit July.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Year in review: right metatarsal osteomyelitis (MSSA) treated and healed by July. Left CRVO in November, retina observing, no edema. Prostate cancer responding, PSA 0.1 last month.
Function: independent in the apartment. Not driving since the eye; uses the van and grocery delivery. No falls.
Mood: PHQ-2 1 - some low days in the winter, nothing more than that he says.
Vaccines up to date (flu/COVID/RSV in the fall, Shingrix complete, PCV20). Tdap not found in registry - offered, he declined today.
LDCT due this month - ordered.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet: right forefoot scar intact, no new lesions; vibration reduced both feet; faint pedal pulses.
Labs: A1c around 9. Kidney function at baseline. Counts normal.
Plan: meds unchanged. RTC 3-4 months.

reports.conclusion: Acalculous acute cholecystitis pattern: wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid, no stones.

reports.text: Supine and upright views of the abdomen. Curvilinear lucencies follow the contour of the gallbladder wall in the right upper quadrant, in keeping with gas in the wall. Nonobstructive bowel gas pattern. No free air.
Specimen: gallbladder. Wall thickened and edematous with transmural acute inflammation and mucosal ulceration. No calculi in the specimen. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Acute acalculous cholecystitis. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: General surgery discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Hospital Discharge Summary - General Surgery
Patient: Lawrence Leary, 68 M
Admitted: 05/13/2025 via the emergency department. Discharged: 05/17/2025.
Diagnosis: acute acalculous cholecystitis with gas in the gallbladder wall.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy 05/14/2025.

Presentation: two days of severe, constant, sharp pain in the right upper abdomen spreading to the right shoulder, with fevers and shaking chills. Background of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, recent right foot osteomyelitis (treated) and left central retinal vein occlusion; also hypertension, CKD 3, PAD, BPH, prostate cancer (suspected per transferred list).
On arrival: temperature 38.9 C (102 F), HR 110, BP 135/85. Marked right upper quadrant tenderness with a positive Murphy sign.
Labs: WBC 18,000, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 250,000, total bilirubin 1.2, alkaline phosphatase 120, AST 50, ALT 45, glucose 300.
Imaging: ultrasound with gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid but no stones; plain film with curvilinear gas in the gallbladder wall.

Course: IV piperacillin-tazobactam, fluids, insulin sliding scale while inpatient. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy the next morning without conversion; gallbladder inflamed, no perforation. Afebrile from postoperative day 1, tolerating diet, pain controlled with acetaminophen. Pathology: acute acalculous cholecystitis, no malignancy.

Home medications on discharge: metformin 1000 mg BID, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily. NEW: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 5 days.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week; general surgery clinic in 2-3 weeks. Return for fever, worsening pain, jaundice or wound drainage.

General Surgery

documents.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Operative Report
Preop/postop dx: acute cholecystitis, acalculous, with gas in the wall.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Anesthesia: general.
Findings: distended, edematous, inflamed gallbladder with surrounding omental adhesions; no perforation, no abscess. Critical view of safety obtained; cystic duct and artery clipped and divided. Gallbladder removed in a retrieval bag via the umbilical port. Hemostasis confirmed.
EBL minimal. No complications. Specimen to pathology.
General Surgery

documents.title: Transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 5/17 after lap chole for acute acalculous cholecystitis (gas in the wall on films). Pathology benign. Finished amox-clav yesterday.
Feels sore at the port sites, eating small meals, bowels moving, no fever. Some fatigue.
Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Port sites clean, no redness or drainage. Abd soft, appropriately tender near the umbilicus.
Meds reconciled against discharge list (hospital list did not include his oncology drugs - he confirms still taking enzalutamide and had leuprolide in April).
Labs today to make sure the white count settled.
Plan: surgical follow-up 6/3. Call for fever or yellowing.

Three weeks after laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acalculous acute cholecystitis. Pathology without malignancy.

Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: incisions healed. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Plan: no restrictions after 6 weeks from surgery. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Vascular surgery discharge summary
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Hospital Discharge Summary - Vascular Surgery
Patient: Lawrence Leary, 69 M
Admitted 11/15/2025 through the ED; discharged 11/26/2025 to an inpatient rehabilitation facility.
Principal diagnosis: infected gangrene of the left lower extremity with critical limb ischemia not amenable to revascularization.
Procedures: diagnostic left leg angiogram 11/17; left below-knee amputation 11/19.

Presentation: two weeks of increasing pain, swelling and redness of the left leg, and a left heel ulcer draining foul material for months. History of poorly controlled diabetes, PAD and a prior right foot osteomyelitis; also hypertension, CKD 3, BPH, angiodysplasia of cecum, CRVO, cholecystitis, prostate cancer (suspected).
Admission: temperature 38.6 C (101.5 F), BP 150/90, pulse 88, RR 18. Left heel ulcer 3 x 4 cm with black eschar and surrounding cellulitis. No palpable left dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial pulse. Diminished sensation both legs.
Labs: WBC 18,000, hemoglobin 12, platelets 250,000, creatinine 1.8, CRP 24 mg/L (normal <5).
Arterial duplex: no flow in the left anterior tibial, posterior tibial or peroneal arteries.

Course: IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Angiogram 11/17 confirmed occlusion of all three tibial vessels with no distal target for bypass or endovascular treatment; popliteal artery patent. Left below-knee amputation 11/19. Fever resolved within 48 hours of surgery and antibiotics were stopped after source control. Creatinine back to about 1.7 by discharge. Insulin sliding scale inpatient. Residual limb incision intact on discharge; staples in place.

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily; NEW oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 one tablet every 6 hours as needed, short supply.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: vascular surgery clinic in 3-4 weeks for staple removal and wound check; primary care after rehab discharge.

Vascular Surgery

documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility - Discharge Summary
Patient: Lawrence Leary
Admit 11/26/2025, discharge 12/12/2025.
Reason: rehabilitation after left below-knee amputation (11/19) for infected gangrene with nonrevascularizable ischemia.
Course: daily PT and OT. Independent with transfers and wheelchair mobility; walks short distances with a walker hopping on the right leg, with standby assist. Residual limb wound healing, staples removed 12/10, shrinker sock started. Pain controlled with acetaminophen; oxycodone no longer needed after the first week.
Medications at discharge: metformin 1000 mg BID, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily, enzalutamide 160 mg daily (patient's own supply).
Allergies: NKDA.
Disposition: home (first-floor apartment) with home health PT/OT and nursing. Wheelchair and walker supplied.
Follow-up: vascular surgery 1/2026; prosthetics evaluation once the limb has matured; primary care within 1 week.
Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

documents.title: Transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in wheelchair. Admitted 11/15 with infected gangrene of the left heel and no reconstructable arteries below the knee; left BKA 11/19. Rehab 11/26-12/12, now home with home health starting this week.
How he is: tired, sleeping ok, phantom sensations at night but not painful. Using acetaminophen only. Getting around the apartment in the chair and with the walker for short hops. Says he was expecting it after the heel turned black.
Meds reconciled: home meds unchanged from before admission. Enzalutamide continues; leuprolide next due in January.
Exam: afebrile. Weight down after the amputation. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Left residual limb: incision closed, no drainage or redness, shrinker on. Right foot: skin intact, no ulcer, faint pulses.
Plan:
- home health PT/OT/RN orders to sign when they arrive.
- check right foot daily - mirror demonstrated.
- vascular f/u in January; prosthetics after.
- labs today.
Talked about how he is coping alone; he wants to stay home and has the van and delivery set up. Will call him next week.
